question: Will a landmark AI paper by a primarily European pool of authors remain unpublished by 08:40 AM PT July 21, 2026?

model.prompt_context:
Resolution criteria:
- "Yes": Wins if, as of 08:40 AM PT on July 21, 2026 (converted to UTC: 15:40 UTC on July 21, 2026), no AI paper meeting the definition of "landmark" and authored primarily by a European pool of authors has been publicly published or released (e.g., on arXiv, a peer-reviewed journal, or an official institutional repository).
- "No": Wins if, by 08:40 AM PT on July 21, 2026 (15:40 UTC on July 21, 2026), at least one AI paper meeting the definition of "landmark" and authored primarily by a European pool of authors has been publicly published or released (e.g., on arXiv, a peer-reviewed journal, or an official institutional repository).

Clarifications:
- "Primarily European pool of authors" means the majority (more than 50%) of listed authors are affiliated with European institutions at the time of publication.
- "Landmark" is interpreted as a paper that has been widely recognized as a major, field-defining contribution to AI research, either through explicit designation by a major AI venue/institution or through contemporaneous widespread coverage by credible scientific news outlets at or before the settlement time.
- Publication date is determined by the official submission or release timestamp on the hosting platform (e.g., arXiv submission date/time in UTC).
